learning_outcomes.text: Identifies and describes basic principles and methods of the mechanical engineering domain.
Explains and interprets theoretical and experimental results, technical documentation, phenomena and processes in the mechanical engineering domain.
Operates with basic methods and techniques from the domain and associates them with specific graphical representations in the mechanical engineering domain.
Selects and applies basic concepts, principles and methods from the domain for mechanical and strength calculations specific to mechanical structures and systems.
Selects and applies evaluation criteria, principles and methods for identifying, modeling, and experimenting with mechanical phenomena and processes.
Develops professional projects of medium complexity by selecting, combining, and utilizing concepts, principles, methodologies, and technologies from the mechanical engineering domain.
Selects and analyzes bibliographic sources specific to the mechanical engineering domain.
Demonstrates autonomy in learning specific issues of the mechanical engineering domain.

syllabus_topics: Introduction
Properties of metallic materials
Industrial production of metallic materials
Theoretical considerations on casting metallic materials
Casting in temporary molds
Casting in durable (metallic) molds
Elaboration and casting of common industrial alloys
Theoretical considerations on plastic deformation processing of metallic materials
Methods and procedures of plastic deformation processing
Welding processing of metallic materials
Related welding procedures
Processing by powder aggregation of materials
Processing of non-metallic materials
Processing of composite materials
Health and safety at work and ecology rules
Health and safety at work rules for processing by casting, plastic deformation, and welding
Manual molding of a part in two frames with a sectioned pattern; manual core molding
Determination of fluidity of cast metallic materials. Determination of linear shrinkage of cast metallic materials
Determination of heating and cooling regime of forgeable metallic materials
Determination of technological parameters for stretching and upsetting by free mechanical forging
Technology of electric arc fusion welding
Calculation of electrode consumption and time norm for welding

assessment_methods.method: Final Exam (including formative and summative tests)

assessment_rules: The final evaluation result is determined by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity. A minimum grade of 5 (five) must be obtained for both the Exam/Colloquium activities and the Laboratory activities separately.
